summary: Lists requirements for version 2 of the Internet Open Trading Protocol, which aims to build on version 1's framework for online commerce while replacing its XML messaging and digital signatures with standards-based mechanisms. It divides features into those that will, may, and will not be included.

eli5.summary: IOTP is a set of rules for buying things online. This document is the wish list for the second version, sorted into things it must, might, and will not do.

questions: what is the internet open trading protocol
what features were planned for iotp version 2
how does iotp v2 differ from v1
what standards does iotp v2 use
subtitle: A roadmap for extending the Internet Open Trading Protocol with modern standards

tldr.problem: Version 1 of the Internet Open Trading Protocol works for online commerce, but its custom XML messaging and digital signature design need updating to use standard technologies.
tldr.mechanism: Version 2 will be a superset of v1, replacing the ad hoc XML and digital signature parts with standards-based mechanisms while extending support for flexible transaction sequences and improved payment handling.
tldr.outcome: IOTP v2 provides a cleaner, more standardized framework for online commerce built on proven technologies rather than custom implementations.

facts.label: Replaces
facts.value: IOTP v1 messaging and signatures only

today: RFC 3354 is Informational and has not been obsoleted. It defines the requirements that IOTP v2 must meet, though the actual v2 specification has not been issued as an RFC.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Internet Open Trading Protocol (IOTP) provides a framework for Internet commerce. Version 1, defined in RFC 2801, works by handling the interchange of transaction information between parties. However, it uses custom-designed XML messaging and digital signature mechanisms that are not standards-based.

Version 2 will extend IOTP v1 while adopting standard technologies: it will replace the ad hoc XML messaging and digital signature parts with standards-based mechanisms, particularly RFC 3275 (XML-Signature Syntax and Processing).
sections.eli5: IOTP v1 is like a store's rulebook for online shopping. IOTP v2 will mostly follow the same rules but will use the same kinds of message envelopes and signature systems that other internet technologies use.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.content:
IOTP v2 follows several core design principles. It must describe the syntax and processing needed to extend the interoperable framework of IOTP v1. The specification will keep changes to v1 to a minimum and maintain all existing functionality. All XML DTDs and Schemas will be tested to ensure they are well-formed.

The protocol is designed to work well with other standards such as ECML (E-Commerce Markup Language). IOTP v2 should embrace the broader Web design philosophy of decentralization, URIs, Web data, and modularity rather than being a monolithic system.
sections.eli5: IOTP v2 keeps everything that worked in v1. It is built to work with other internet standards and follows the internet's philosophy of modular, reusable pieces rather than one big system.

sections.title: Requirements for Version 2
sections.content:
IOTP v2 has several required features. It must be a superset of v1, preserving all existing functionality. It will provide dynamic definition of trading sequences, meaning transactions will no longer be limited to one payment and one delivery as in v1. Instead, arbitrary sequences of transaction steps can be proposed and processed.

Additional requirements include specification of an Offer Request Block, support for improved problem resolution (such as presenting signed receipts to customer support), provisions to indicate and handle payment protocols that bypass IOTP, and support for server-based wallets. Optional features may include repeated or ongoing payments with spending limits, enhanced server-to-server messages to track shipment status, and the ability to add both fields and attributes to existing trading blocks.
sections.eli5: IOTP v2 must do everything v1 does. It adds the ability to do more complex purchase sequences, better handling of problems, wallets stored on servers, and possibly recurring charges with limits.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.content:
Certain areas are explicitly outside the scope of IOTP v2. Legal and regulatory issues surrounding protocol implementation are left to others. Design of an XML Messaging Layer is out of scope; instead, whatever becomes the standard XML messaging layer will be adopted. Similarly, design of XML Digital Signatures is out of scope; the specification will use the existing standard RFC 3275.

This approach keeps IOTP v2 focused on commerce semantics rather than building infrastructure that other standards handle.
sections.eli5: IOTP v2 does not make up its own rules for sending messages or checking signatures. It will use whatever standard systems already exist for those jobs.
